findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === instead of .isSame(), always evaluates to false
findings.body: The expression `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` uses strict equality (`===`) to compare two Dayjs object instances. This always returns `false` because `===` compares object references, not date values. The intent is to detect "unavailable all day" date overrides (where start equals end). Because this check never passes, such overrides will not correctly block all slots on that day. Use `.isSame()` instead.

findings.title: Copy-paste error: `end` uses slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
findings.body: The variable `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, which is identical to `start` on the line above. It should use `slotEndTime` to correctly check whether the slot's end time exceeds the working hours boundary. As written, a slot whose end time extends past the working hours end time will not be detected as out-of-bounds, potentially showing unavailable slots as bookable.

findings.title: Working hours check incorrectly rejects slots when multiple ranges exist for the same day
findings.body: The `workingHours.find(...)` logic returns `false` (unavailable) if the slot is outside ANY single working hour range for that day. If a user has multiple working hour ranges (e.g., 9–12 and 14–17), a slot at 10:00 is within the first range but outside the second. The `find` will match the second range and incorrectly mark the slot as unavailable. The correct logic should return `false` only if the slot is not within ANY working hour range for that day (i.e., use `!workingHours.some(...)` or equivalent).

findings.title: override.timeZone may be undefined, causing incorrect offset calculation
findings.body: The `TimeRange` type defines `timeZone` as optional (`timeZone?: string`). In `slots.ts`, the code calls `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` without guarding against `override.timeZone` being `undefined`. When `undefined` is passed to `.tz()`, dayjs may fall back to the system's local timezone or behave unpredictably, producing an incorrect UTC offset and thus wrong slot times. A fallback (e.g., to `organizerTimeZone`) should be provided.

findings.title: No test for the primary fix: round-robin with fixed hosts and date overrides
findings.body: The PR description states the main fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts are now taken into account for round-robin events, preventing bookings where fixed hosts are unavailable. However, no test is added that creates a round-robin event with a fixed host, sets a date override on that fixed host, and verifies that only slots within the override are shown. The only added test checks timezone adjustment for a personal event, not the round-robin + fixed host scenario.
